text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/exposed-design-a.md <<'EOF'
# Candidate A: committed SQLx metadata and atomic publication

## Usage and problem

A relevant push to main produces `ghcr.io/johnnylarner/exposed:yyyy.mm.dd.hh.mm` and a matching GitHub release. The release gives the full source SHA, image digest, and `docker run --env DATABASE_URL=... -p 6999:6999 ghcr.io/johnnylarner/exposed@sha256:...`. Operators apply migrations separately, as db/README.md requires. Default image entrypoint is `exposed`, command `server`; data CLI remains available through command overrides.

Grounding: one Rust workspace member, exposed, with one binary at exposed/src/bin/main.rs. SQLx 0.9 query macros depend on migrated PostgreSQL; application startup does not migrate. Server listens on 6999. Cargo.toml declares MSRV 1.94 but requested build toolchain is 1.98.1. No existing workflows or Dockerfile found.

## Shape

Files: root Dockerfile and .dockerignore; committed root .sqlx metadata; .github/workflows/release.yml; one small scripts/release script owning tag allocation, immutable digest association, and retry reconciliation; README instructions for metadata refresh and image operation. Keep complex release state transitions out of shell snippets scattered across workflow steps.

Docker uses pinned Rust 1.98.1 Debian builder plus pinned cargo-chef version. Planner emits recipe from workspace; chef cooks release dependencies with `--locked` into ordinary image layers; builder copies source and .sqlx, sets SQLX_OFFLINE=true, builds exposed. Use `cache-from/to: type=gha,scope=exposed-linux-amd64,mode=max`. Do not put Cargo target under a BuildKit cache mount: dependency objects must survive export to a fresh hosted runner through the cooked layer. Scope initial architecture to linux/amd64 unless multiarch is explicitly required. Pin runtime base by digest and use matching Debian generation, CA certificates, actual shared libraries discovered with ldd, numeric nonroot UID/GID, /app workdir, exposed port 6999, exec-form entrypoint. Exclude .env, .git, target, frontend, ingest, data, captures from context. Include only binary and required runtime resources in final stage.

CI starts pinned PG18 service, installs pinned SQLx CLI0.9, runs the real migrations, and checks committed metadata with cargo sqlx prepare --check --workspace -- --all-targets. Initial metadata generation is a one-time developer action against isolated migrated PG18 and subsequent query changes refresh it. Docker remains independently buildable offline; validation uses real schema. Pin action revisions to immutable SHAs and container bases/services to verified digests; avoid invented digest values. Global token permissions contents:read; publication job alone gets contents:write/packages:write. Checkout persist-credentials:false; GHCR login uses GITHUB_TOKEN. Never send DATABASE_URL into Docker build args.

Trigger on main push for exposed/** and all build inputs: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, .sqlx/**, db/migrations/**, sqlx.toml, Dockerfile, .dockerignore, release workflow/script, toolchain config if added. Each push head gets one release; a multi-commit push is one event. Path trigger semantics should be explicit: this includes build-affecting changes outside exposed.

Publication state owns tuple `(source_sha, tag, image_digest)`:
1. Build and push a staging image addressed by the source SHA; resolve output manifest digest. A rerun reuses the previously pinned source image instead of silently replacing an established release with a rebuild.
2. Atomically create annotated git tag `date -u +%Y.%m.%d.%H.%M` at the exact push SHA, with machine-readable immutable image digest in annotation. This binds source and image before release creation. Existing same-SHA reservation resumes; another SHA owning current minute means wait for next real UTC minute and retry. Concurrent create conflict is expected; fetch and inspect winner. Do not fabricate future minute values or append suffixes, both change date contract.
3. Add timestamp image tag pointing to reserved digest, verify registry digest, then create/update GitHub release for that git tag. Existing matching release is success. Conflicting release/source/digest is hard failure. Release body contains canonical digest pull reference and source permalink.

No global concurrency group: every push can build and atomically reserve its own publication minute. Timestamp namespace inherently permits at most one distinct release per minute. Optional per-SHA group suppresses duplicate runs only; it must not cancel distinct push heads. Existing default Actions concurrency keeps only one pending run, so it loses pushes. GitHub now also supports queue:max, but it is bounded and should not be advertised as an unbounded durable queue.

A crash after image push leaves harmless staging object. Crash after tag reservation leaves persistent source/digest state that reruns finish. Crash after release creation is already complete. Do not delete reservations on errors, overwrite published tags, or use release creation time as retry identity. Before selecting current minute, search existing version tags by exact source SHA to recover an earlier reservation. Force pushes/repeated same-head pushes require stated policy: one release per unique source commit; if literally one per event is required, persist run_id in annotation and use that as recovery identity.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Accept committed generated metadata and a schema freshness check in exchange for a standalone Docker build without live PG or CI artifacts. CI-generated metadata avoids tracked files but makes Docker build depend on a preceding service-backed preparation step and repeats compilation outside Docker; reject as default. Database inside Docker build adds process lifecycle/network complexity and defeats clean separation.

Accept a short release-state script in exchange for retries that converge after every publication boundary. A one-line gh release create plus date command is smaller but leaves collisions, unpublished images, and reruns unspecified. A globally serialized queue is viable with queue:max, but bounded pending capacity plus builds holding the lock weakens every-push behavior; reserve atomically instead.

Accept Debian runtime footprint over scratch/musl until native dependencies and TLS behavior are proven. Do not claim static linking from Rust alone.

## Checks and unresolved details

Verify clean metadata check; cold Docker build with SQLX_OFFLINE and no DB connectivity; warm rebuild after source-only edit showing chef layer cache hit on fresh BuildKit; image --help as nonroot; real server startup/query against migrated PG18; shared-library inspection; release script tests simulating collision and failure at each publication boundary. Explicitly verify deployed server port fallback behavior before labeling runtime production-ready: current server falls back to arbitrary port on address-in-use.

This design requires checking Rust1.98.1 image availability and all pins during implementation, measuring dependency build memory requirements (Polars/Arrow), and checking CLI0.9 prepare option behavior against official docs. No implementation or pins are claimed verified here.

Sources: Docker cache exports https://docs.docker.com/build/cache/backends/ and https://docs.docker.com/build/cache/backends/gha/; GitHub concurrency https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/concurrency and new larger queue https://github.blog/changelog/2026-05-07-github-actions-concurrency-groups-now-allow-larger-queues/ .
EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));

content.text:
Wrote candidate design to `/tmp/exposed-design-a.md`.

Recommends committed SQLx metadata, exported cargo-chef layers, nonroot Debian runtime, and atomic timestamp tag reservations carrying the immutable image digest for retry recovery. Flags minute-level throughput, per-push versus per-commit identity, and current server port fallback.

Current GitHub supports `concurrency.queue: max`; default pending replacement remains unsafe for every-push publication.
